root.text: Akerson turns from the mirror with the timing of a man who has practised turning from mirrors. The smile arrives before the eye contact does. "You know, people say to me, John, how do you do it, and I tell them: you don't *do* it. You *are* it." He lets that land on you like it's a gift. "Anyway. You wanted something."

n_show.text: "The show." He says it the way other men say their children's names. "Forty minutes, live, no net. Everyone in this building has a job and mine is the only one that can't be done by somebody else." He waits. There is clearly a follow-up question he would like you to ask.

n_ratings.text: "*Numbers.*" A short laugh, entirely for his own benefit. "I stopped reading them years ago. Obviously I know them. I just don't *read* them." He adjusts a cuff that did not need adjusting. "Second in the slot. Behind a channel that runs executions. That's not a ratings problem, that's a *civilisation* problem."

n_notnow.text: He holds up one finger without looking at you, the gesture of a man silencing a room he assumes is listening. "Not now. I'm on in a few and I don't hand out anything good before a show. Voice goes flat when I give something away for free." He is already facing the lights again. "Catch me off the clock. I'm significantly more generous when nobody's watching, which is one of the great ironies of my life."

n_recipe.text:
"*Cook.*" He says it like you've mispronounced something. "I don't cook. I have three dishes and one of them is famous, which is a better ratio than any chef in this city can claim."

He leans in. This is the part he likes.

"Penne alla gin. And before you say it: yes, it's meant to be vodka. Vodka is *nothing*, it's a rumour with a proof rating. Gin has an opinion. You cook the tomato down until it stops being a vegetable, you take the pan *off the heat*, you put the gin in, and the alcohol leaves and the whole hedge stays behind."

options.label: Sounds like a lot of talk.

n_barb.text: "It *is* a lot of talk. That's the job." He seems genuinely pleased with you for the first time. "But I've fed that pasta to two network heads and a woman who owns a moon, and not one of them left. Say what you like about me, and people do, at length, it's a whole genre. The sauce works."

n_teach.text: He talks you through it twice, the second time slower, and both times he manages to mention the woman who owns the moon. "Pan, not a pot. You want it wide enough that the water leaves. Penne, because the ridges hold the sauce and smooth pasta is for people who don't finish things. Tomato, hard, until it darkens. Gin *off the heat* unless you want a fire and a story. Cream last, and stop stirring before you think you should." He straightens up, done, and checks his reflection to see how the teaching looked on him. "There. Now two of us can make it. Don't let that get around."

n_thanks.text: "*Thanks.*" He waves it off with real discomfort, the first honest thing he's done all conversation. "Just... if it comes out well, say where you got it. Not for me. For the *record*."

bye.text: "Mm." He has already returned to the mirror. "Tell them I was taller than you expected."

home_activities: pours two fingers of something amber and pointedly does not offer you any
"Forty-fourth floor. You can't hear the city scream from up here. That's the whole point."
sprawls back on the emperor bed and scrolls last night's ratings on a floating screen, smirking
practises a monologue punchline to the window, nails it, and toasts his own reflection
"I've interviewed presidents, killers, and one very rude AI. Sit down before you embarrass us both."
lets a silk robe hang open and watches the bay lights without really seeing them
signs a glossy headshot of himself, props it on the bar, and steps back to admire the work
"Room service up here is a helicopter. I'm not joking. Ask me about the helicopter."
cranks something with a heavy bassline and air-drums the bridge, entirely unashamed
"The trick to the desk is never letting them see you sweat. The trick to the penthouse is never letting them up."
thumbs a tab of Neural Overclock onto his tongue like a breath mint and carries on as though you didn't see it
"Everyone in this business runs on something. I just have better taste in mine than the rest of them."
rubs a smear of Overclock into his gums mid-sentence, barely breaking stride
name: John Akerson
